evals.title: Evidence-driven PTO optimization plans for each case
evals.prompt: Use tilelang-perf-optimize to develop performance optimization plans for a PTO Reduction kernel in the current repository. Latency and profiling metrics are available for every case, but different shapes enter different dispatch branches. Explain the analysis sequence, how to invoke tilelang-performance-best-practices, and what the final plans must contain. Do not execute external tools.
evals.expected_output: First fix the repository, actual TileLang/PTOAS environment, and measurement methodology. Then map every case to its real dispatch branch and group cases by semantics, dtype, tail handling, and bottleneck. Build models for core count, tiles, buffer versions, padding, reads/writes, and reduction state. Candidates must be supported by evidence and checked against the APIs and lowering through tilelang-performance-best-practices. Matching references/*/code/*_asc.py files may supply host and kernel structures without maturity registration; maturity is required only when reusing an executable template. Output at most three admitted plans with status IMPLEMENTABLE or EXPERIMENT, covering all cases and including parameters, validation commands, performance methodology, and rollback conditions. List DESIGN_ONLY items separately as non-admitted candidates; they do not count toward the limit and must not be handed off for implementation.

expectations.name: maps_every_case_to_real_branch
expectations.description: Analyze each case using its real execution path
expectations.assertion_text: Every case is mapped to its actual dispatch/kernel branch and appears in the coverage table

expectations.name: uses_tilelang_feasibility_gate
expectations.description: Use the implementation-knowledge skill to verify feasibility
expectations.assertion_text: Load tilelang-performance-best-practices and filter candidates against the target repository, actual TileLang source, and PTO lowering; source-reading _asc.py references require no maturity entry, while executable templates retain their maturity gate

expectations.name: limits_and_validates_plans
expectations.description: State plan-count limits and validation conditions clearly
expectations.assertion_text: Provide at most three admitted IMPLEMENTABLE/EXPERIMENT plans, each with evidence, parameters, applicable cases, correctness and performance validation, and rollback conditions; list DESIGN_ONLY items separately and do not hand them off for implementation

evals.title: Do not speculate when profiling evidence is missing
evals.prompt: Use tilelang-perf-optimize to analyze a TileLang/PTO elementwise kernel. The user provided only the source and the statement 'performance is very poor'; they supplied no per-case latency, profiling data, or test cases. How should you proceed? Do not execute external tools.
evals.expected_output: Explain that the available evidence is insufficient. First collect the public interface and complete target case set, confirm baseline correctness and PTO compilation, verify the target kernel, and then collect per-case latency and available profiling under identical conditions. Until the data is available, provide only a collection plan or hypotheses to validate; do not claim a VEC/MEM/SCALAR bound or prescribe definitive tile parameters or an expected speedup.

expectations.name: does_not_invent_bottleneck
expectations.description: Do not conclude a bound without evidence
expectations.assertion_text: Without per-case profiling, do not claim a specific bound; output only a data-collection plan and hypotheses to validate

expectations.name: requires_complete_case_scope
expectations.description: Establish the target cases and baseline first
expectations.assertion_text: Require the complete case set, baseline correctness, PTO compilation status, and per-case latency collected under identical conditions

evals.title: Do not treat a lower-level capability as a TileLang API
evals.prompt: An optimization proposal proves only that PTOAS internally supports an instruction, but no corresponding frontend API or lowering example can be found in the current TileLang source, examples/ascend, or the current repository. Use tilelang-perf-optimize to decide whether this proposal may enter a directly implementable plan. Do not execute external tools.
evals.expected_output: It cannot enter a directly implementable plan. PTOAS capability does not prove that the TileLang frontend can express it. Continue verification in the actually imported TileLang source, lowering, and runnable Python implementations. If no evidence is found, mark it DESIGN_ONLY, list it separately as a non-admitted candidate, do not count it toward the maximum of three admitted plans, and specify the API, lowering, correctness, and performance evidence still required.

expectations.name: separates_frontend_from_backend
expectations.description: Distinguish the TileLang frontend from PTOAS
expectations.assertion_text: An internal PTOAS capability does not imply that the TileLang frontend already exposes a usable API

expectations.name: marks_unverified_as_design_only
expectations.description: Do not directly implement an unverified candidate
expectations.assertion_text: When no current-source or lowering evidence exists, mark the item DESIGN_ONLY, list it separately as a non-admitted candidate, exclude it from the admitted-plan limit, and require additional validation evidence

evals.title: Current source evidence is not restricted by template registration
evals.prompt: The current branch of the repository contains a runnable TileLang/PTO implementation: its API and lowering can be located in the actual TileLang source, and it passes correctness checks on the target cases, but tilelang-performance-best-practices has not yet registered it in template_status.md. Use tilelang-perf-optimize to determine whether it can support an optimization plan. Do not execute external tools.
evals.expected_output: Do not downgrade it to DESIGN_ONLY solely because it is absent from the template status table. The current repository and actual TileLang source are direct factual sources. If the bottleneck evidence, API, lowering, correctness, applicable cases, and validation method are complete, classify it independently as IMPLEMENTABLE or EXPERIMENT. A source-reading _asc.py reference records only its internal path and requires no maturity; path and maturity are mandatory when reusing a bundled executable template. An unregistered implementation must not be presented as a validated template.

expectations.name: prefers_direct_source_evidence
expectations.description: Prefer current direct source evidence over template registration
expectations.assertion_text: API, lowering, and correctness evidence from the current repository or actual TileLang source can independently admit a plan; absence from template_status.md must not automatically downgrade it to DESIGN_ONLY

expectations.name: still_gates_bundled_templates
expectations.description: The template-maturity gate applies to executable templates, not source-reading code references
expectations.assertion_text: A bundled references/*/code/*_asc.py file may be used as implementation-reading material without maturity, while a bundled executable template still requires its actual path and maturity

evals.title: Performance cases require explicit user confirmation
evals.prompt: Use tilelang-perf-optimize for a kernel that already has cases from operator generation, accuracy validation, and ST. The user asks to start performance tuning but has not submitted or confirmed any performance cases. May those existing cases be used as the performance-case set by default? Explain how to proceed. Do not execute external tools.
evals.expected_output: Stop at the Case Input Gate. Cases from operator generation, accuracy validation, or ST are not performance-tuning cases by default, even if they have already run or have profiling data. Ask the user to submit or explicitly confirm the performance cases before tuning analysis begins. Keep existing correctness cases available for regression validation after optimization, but do not let them expand the performance-case set.

expectations.name: requires_explicit_performance_case_confirmation
expectations.description: Do not infer the performance workload from correctness-oriented cases
expectations.assertion_text: Stop at the Case Input Gate and require the user to submit or explicitly confirm performance cases; do not default to generation, accuracy-validation, or ST cases

expectations.name: keeps_correctness_cases_as_regression_only
expectations.description: Preserve correctness coverage without changing tuning scope
expectations.assertion_text: Existing correctness cases may remain regression inputs after optimization, but they do not expand the user-confirmed performance-case set
